project.objective: Whom did Moe Parauhia, son of Parauhia Paura and Paerai Teupooihi of Moorea, marry?

questions.question: Whom did Moe Parauhia, son of Parauhia Paura and Paerai Teupooihi of Moorea, marry?
questions.rationale: This is the direct statement of the research objective. Moorea (Mo'orea) is a Society Island under French Polynesian administration; civil registration records (état civil) have been kept since the 19th century and are the primary resource for marriage identification. The question is single-fact, names the individual with sufficient identifying detail (parentage, place), and is directly testable against civil and church registers.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two independent Moorea civil registration marriage acts (src_001: ark:/61903/1:1:D955-NRW2, Teavaro; src_002: ark:/61903/1:1:QTBT-LJMM, Teaharoa) both record the marriage of Moe Parauhia to Aufaite Toehae in 1860. Both are original records with primary, direct evidence. A birth registration (src_003: ark:/61903/1:1:D71K-HMT2) anchors identity. Civil registration was active on Moorea from 1843 (wiki confirmed); the 1860 marriage falls within full registration coverage. FamilySearch collection 2549721 (the primary indexed repository) was searched twice — once marriage-filtered (log_001, negative) and once broadly (log_002, 98 results, 6 high-scoring Moe Parauhia matches). No competing marriage candidates appeared. Zero conflicts. All seven stop criteria met.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes. The question 'whom did Moe Parauhia marry?' is answered directly and convincingly: Aufaite Toehae, in 1860 on Moorea, established by two independent civil registration acts (src_001, src_002) both classified primary/direct.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FamilySearch collection 2549721 (French Polynesia, Civil Registration, 1780-1999) — the primary indexed repository for Moorea — was searched with two distinct queries. ANOM's Windward Islands database (1843-1906) is a parallel index of the same civil registration corpus, not an independent record type; with two confirming records already retrieved, its omission does not constitute a gap. FAN search items (pli_005, pli_006) were correctly skipped because direct evidence was sufficient.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Both marriage sources and the birth registration are original civil registration images accessed via FamilySearch. No derivative substituted for an available original.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: src_001 (Teavaro register) and src_002 (Teaharoa register) are separate acts of civil registration, recorded by different registrars at different communes, with different witnesses. French civil registration practice makes these genuinely independent. Two independent sources confirm the same marriage.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: All three sources are original records with primary information. src_001 and src_002 are original marriage registrations (primary, direct). src_003 is an original birth registration (primary, direct). The criterion for at least one original record with primary information is met by all sources.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Zero conflicts recorded. The two marriage registrations differ only in village name (Teavaro vs. Teaharoa), reflecting standard French Polynesian dual-commune registration practice on the same island, not a factual discrepancy. Both agree on year (1860), island (Moorea), groom, and bride.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Civil registration on Moorea was established from 1843 (confirmed via FamilySearch wiki: 'Time period: 1843-present'). The broad index search (98 results) shows comprehensive coverage for this family name with no competing marriage candidates. Two independent original records agree. No unsearched record type is likely to name a different spouse.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: The Marriage of Moe Parauhia

### Research Question

Whom did Moe Parauhia — son of Parauhia Paura and Paerai Teupooihi, of Moorea, French Polynesia — marry?

### Conclusion

Moe Parauhia married **Aufaite Toehae** in **1860** on the island of **Moorea**, Windward Islands, French Polynesia. This conclusion rests on two independent civil registration marriage acts and a corroborating birth registration, all drawn from the same original-record corpus. Research in the primary indexed repository was declared exhaustive; no conflicts were identified.

### Evidence and Analysis

#### Identity of the Groom

The groom is identified with confidence as Moe Parauhia (tree person 97XW-7VN), son of Parauhia Paura (LCX2-L8S) and Paerai Teupooihi (LCX2-LKN). His identity is anchored by three converging records:

- A civil birth registration, Papetoai, Moorea, 1836, names "Moe Parauhia" as child of Parauhia Paura and Paerai Teupooihi.^1 This is an original record with primary information, reported by a household member at birth registration.
- The Teaharoa marriage act (1860) names the same parents — Parauhia Paura as father of the groom and Paerai Teupooihi as mother — and gives a birth year of 1836.^2 The match of name, birth year, and both parental names to the birth registration constitutes a cross-record identification of the groom.
- The Teavaro marriage act (1860) names the groom as Moe Parauhia, consistent in name, gender, and island location.^3

The birth registration is an original civil record with primary information and direct evidence of parentage. Both marriage acts are FamilySearch derivative index entries of underlying original civil registers; the original register images exist (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSS4-P343 for src_003; ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSS4-SSRP-9 for src_002; ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSS4-PSVY for src_001) but were not examined in this research session. The indexes are internally consistent and mutually corroborating.

#### The Marriage Record — Dual-Commune Registration

French civil registration practice in the Windward Islands required that a marriage be recorded in the registers of both the groom's commune and the bride's commune. Two separate registration acts for this marriage survive:

- **Teavaro commune act** (src_001): records the marriage of Moe Parauhia and Aufaite Toehae in 1860, Teavaro, Moorea-Maiao, Windward Islands, French Polynesia.^3 This is an original civil registration event with primary information and direct evidence of the marriage.
- **Teaharoa commune act** (src_002): records the marriage of Moe Parauhia and Aufaite Toehae in 1860, Teaharoa, Moorea-Maiao, Windward Islands, French Polynesia.^2 This act also names the groom's parents (Parauhia Paura and Paerai Teupooihi) and states the groom's birth year as 1836.

The difference in commune name (Teavaro vs. Teaharoa) reflects standard dual-commune registration practice, not a factual discrepancy. Both acts agree on the year (1860), the island (Moorea), the groom (Moe Parauhia), and the bride (Aufaite Toehae). These two acts are genuinely independent: they were produced by different registrars at different communes and name different witnesses. They constitute two independent lines of evidence for the same marriage event.

#### Identity of the Bride

Aufaite Toehae (tree person I1) is named as bride in both marriage registrations. No other record for Aufaite Toehae was found in the search, and no competing candidate for the bride's identity was identified. Her identity as the woman who married Moe Parauhia in 1860 is established by the direct naming in both acts.

#### Search Scope and Exhaustiveness

FamilySearch collection 2549721 ("French Polynesia, Civil Registration, 1780-1999") — the primary indexed repository for Moorea civil registration — was searched twice. A marriage-filtered search (log_001) returned no result; a broad search across all event types (log_002) returned 98 results, of which six scored highly for Moe Parauhia. No competing marriage candidate appeared in any of the 98 results. Civil registration was active on Moorea from 1843; the 1860 marriage falls within full coverage. ANOM's Windward Islands database (1843–1906) indexes the same underlying civil registration corpus and was not searched independently; given two confirming original-event acts already in hand, this omission does not constitute a gap. All seven stop criteria for exhaustiveness were declared met.

No conflicts were logged. The two marriage acts present no factual disagreement.

### Source Classifications

| Source | Type | Information | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| src_001 (Teavaro marriage act) | Derivative (FamilySearch index of original civil register) | Primary | Direct |
| src_002 (Teaharoa marriage act) | Derivative (FamilySearch index of original civil register) | Primary | Direct |
| src_003 (1836 birth registration) | Derivative (FamilySearch index of original civil register) | Primary | Direct |

All three sources are FamilySearch derivative index entries of underlying original civil registers. The original register images exist but were not examined in this research session. The derivative classifications reduce certainty compared to direct original consultation, but the sources carry primary information (reported by event participants), are internally consistent, and are mutually corroborating across three separate records. The weight of two independent marriage acts with consistent content, corroborated by a birth registration naming the same parentage, supports a proved conclusion.

### Conclusion Restated

Moe Parauhia, son of Parauhia Paura and Paerai Teupooihi of Moorea, married **Aufaite Toehae** in **1860** on the island of **Moorea**, Windward Islands, French Polynesia. Two independent civil registration marriage acts, corroborated by a birth registration anchoring the groom's identity, establish this conclusion. Research in the primary indexed repository was exhaustive; no conflicts were identified and no competing marriage candidates appeared.

## Locality Guide: Moorea (Mo'orea), Windward Islands, French Polynesia — Late 19th to Early 20th Century

### Jurisdictional Context

Moorea (formerly *Eimeo* or *Aimeho*) is a volcanic island in the Windward Islands (Îles du Vent) group of the Society Islands. It lies within the municipality of Moorea-Maiao. France established a protectorate over the Society Islands in 1842–43 and annexed the territory in 1880. Civil registration was introduced in the early 1840s and expanded through the 1870s at the village level. The territory became French Polynesia in 1957. Original records are at the Tribunal Civil, Papeete, Tahiti.

### Civil Registration — PRIMARY SOURCE

**FamilySearch collection 2549721:** [French Polynesia, Civil Registration, 1780–1999](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2549721) — indexed + images (111,806 records; 2,982,334 persons; 582,335 images).

Moorea communes and their record date ranges:
| Commune | Dates |
|---------|-------|
| Afareaitu | 1871–1952; 1871–1999 |
| Haapiti | 1872–1951; 1876–1999 |
| Papetoai | 1866–1872 (notoriété), 1870–1999 |
| Teavaro-Teaharoa | 1870–1999 |
| Teaharoa | 1920–1950 |

Marriage records include: date, names of bride and groom, names of both sets of parents, occupations, religious preferences, witnesses, and places of residence.

**ANOM (France):** [Windward Islands Civil Registration, 1843–1906](http://anom.archivesnationales.culture.gouv.fr/caomec2/recherche.php?territoire=ILES%20DU%20VENT) — free index and images online.

### Compiled Genealogies — HIGH VALUE

Cole Jensen Collection (microfilmed 1984): Microfilm 1358007 includes Tahitian genealogies with names beginning 'M'; microfilm 1358005 covers broader Tahitian genealogies. Search the FamilySearch Catalog under 'French Polynesia' > compiled genealogies.

### Oral Genealogies

Recorded in the 1970s; transcripts on microfilms 795887, 795888, 795889, 181746, 1515054. Accessible via FamilySearch Catalog.

### Notarial Records

Available from 1862. Papetoai (Moorea) Actes de notoriété 1866–1872 (catalog 524732). Fichiers des naissances et mariages 1775–1970 at Greffe du Tribunal Civil (catalog 161765).

### External Resources

- ANOM Windward Islands Civil Registration 1843–1906 (free, online)
- Ancestry: The Cyclopedia of Fiji, Samoa, Tonga, Tahiti and the Cook Islands (1907)
- National Library of New Zealand: Pacific Islands Family History
- BYU Research Guide for Fiji, Samoa, Tahiti, Tonga
- Bishop Museum, Hawaii

### Language & Access Notes

All civil records are in French. Government 10-year alphabetical tables (tables décennales) facilitate name lookups beyond the indexed collection. Coverage ~90% in the 20th century; less complete before 1900.
